part.text:
All 17 tests pass and `go vet` is clean. ## What I did The spec in `.docs/instructions.md` is the classic refactoring exercise: make the parser easier to read and maintain while keeping every test green. I rewrote `markdown.go` (the only file changed) from a byte-at-a-time scanner into a line-based parser: - **`Render`** now splits the input into lines and dispatches each line to a small renderer — `renderHeader`, `renderListItem`, or `renderParagraph` — instead of the original loop that jumbled four pieces of state (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`) with position arithmetic and `LastIndex` tricks. - **List grouping** is tracked with a single `inList` boolean: consecutive `* ` lines share one `
    `, and the list closes when a non-item line appears or at end of input. - **`headerLevel`** counts leading `#`s; levels 1–6 render as `…`, while 7+ fall through to a paragraph (matching the tested `#######` behavior). - **`renderEmphasis`** keeps the original semantics exactly: at most one `__…__` pair becomes `` and one `_…_` pair becomes ``, applied to the text of each block. Behavioral notes, documented in comments: a trailing newline is trimmed so it doesn't produce an empty `

    `, and `#`/`*` symbols appearing inside header, list-item, or paragraph text are left literal — which is what the "markdown symbols should not be interpreted" test cases require. `markdown_test.go` and `cases_test.go` are untouched, and no new files were created.
